youtube.title: What Really Happened to TOMS Shoes?
youtube.description:
TOMS promised a free pair of shoes to a child for every pair it sold, and said it gave away close to 100 million. So why, in December 2019, did its lenders end up owning the company?

This documentary follows the evidence: the 2014 Bain Capital deal that valued TOMS at $625 million, the loan that came with it, a randomized study of the donated shoes, and the sneaker shift that left a canvas slip-on behind. One decision, and what it cost.

{CHAPTERS}

How this was made: an original script, researched and fact-checked from the sources above. Maps, charts and graphics are our own; some footage is licensed stock, and scenes no camera filmed are illustrations made with AI tools. The narration is a synthetic voice.

sources.claim: In December 2019 TOMS was handed to its lenders, who swapped about $300 million of debt for ownership
sources.source: Bloomberg and The Wall Street Journal reporting on the TOMS debt restructuring, December 2019

sources.claim: The lenders included Jefferies, Searchlight Capital and Nexus Capital
sources.source: Bloomberg, December 2019

sources.claim: The loan of roughly $300 million was due in 2020
sources.source: Bloomberg, December 2019; Moody's rating actions on TOMS Shoes LLC term loan

sources.claim: TOMS said it had given away close to 100 million pairs, more than 95 million by 2019
sources.source: TOMS company announcements, 2019

sources.claim: Bain Capital bought half of TOMS in August 2014 at a $625 million valuation
sources.source: The New York Times DealBook and Bloomberg, 20 August 2014

sources.claim: The founder kept half and said he would put half his proceeds into a fund for social entrepreneurs
sources.source: The New York Times DealBook, 20 August 2014

sources.claim: Both sides said the one-for-one promise would continue after the deal
sources.source: TOMS and Bain Capital statements, August 2014

sources.claim: Moody's rated a term loan of roughly $300 million taken on by TOMS in the 2014 deal
sources.source: Moody's Investors Service rating action, TOMS Shoes LLC, 2014

sources.claim: Rating agencies downgraded TOMS's debt as results weakened
sources.source: Moody's Investors Service rating actions, 2016-2019

sources.claim: In 2006 the founder travelled to Argentina, saw children without shoes, and based TOMS on the alpargata
sources.source: Blake Mycoskie, Start Something That Matters (2011)

sources.claim: TOMS is short for 'Tomorrow's Shoes'; the first pairs were made by shoemakers in Argentina
sources.source: Blake Mycoskie, Start Something That Matters (2011)

sources.claim: A Los Angeles Times story in 2006 brought 2,200 orders in a day
sources.source: Blake Mycoskie, Start Something That Matters (2011)

sources.claim: TOMS sold 10,000 pairs in its first summer and gave 10,000 pairs in Argentina that autumn
sources.source: Blake Mycoskie, Start Something That Matters (2011)

sources.claim: TOMS gave its one millionth pair in 2010 and its ten millionth in 2013
sources.source: TOMS company announcements, September 2010 and June 2013

sources.claim: TOMS Eyewear launched in 2011 with a sight-restoration pledge
sources.source: TOMS announcement, June 2011

sources.claim: Skechers launched BOBS in 2010 with its own donation pledge
sources.source: Skechers USA annual report (10-K), 2010

sources.claim: In 2013 TOMS pledged to make a third of its giving shoes in the countries receiving them, including Haiti, Kenya, Ethiopia and India
sources.source: TOMS announcement, 2013; reported by Fast Company, 2013

sources.claim: A University of San Francisco randomized study in rural El Salvador found little measurable effect on children's overall health, and recipients slightly more likely to agree others should provide for their family
sources.source: Wydick, Katz, Calvo, Gutierrez and Janet, 'Shoeing the Children', World Bank Economic Review, 2018

sources.claim: Researchers also tested whether donations hurt local shoe sellers and found a small negative effect
sources.source: Wydick, Katz and Janet, Journal of Development Effectiveness, 2014

sources.claim: TOMS opened its giving programme to the researchers
sources.source: Wydick et al., World Bank Economic Review, 2018

sources.claim: TOMS Roasting Co. launched in 2014: each bag funded a week of clean water
sources.source: TOMS announcement, March 2014

sources.claim: TOMS bags launched in 2015, funding safe-birth help
sources.source: TOMS announcement, 2015

sources.claim: In a 2016 essay the founder wrote that he had stepped away after losing his passion for the work
sources.source: Blake Mycoskie, Harvard Business Review, January-February 2016

sources.claim: A new chief executive took over day-to-day leadership in 2015
sources.source: TOMS announcement of Jim Alling as CEO, 2015

sources.claim: Shoppers moved to sneakers and athletic styles; cheaper lookalikes competed with TOMS
sources.source: Bloomberg, December 2019; Moody's rating commentary, 2016-2019

sources.claim: In 2019 TOMS replaced one-for-one with giving one third of profits: '1/3 of profits for grassroots good'
sources.source: TOMS announcement, 2019

sources.claim: Warby Parker began 'Buy a Pair, Give a Pair' in 2010 and went public in 2021
sources.source: Warby Parker Form S-1 registration statement, August 2021

sources.claim: US interest rates were near zero in 2014
sources.source: US Federal Reserve, federal funds rate history, 2014
